tagline: A painters' boarding house and a tavern Washington danced in.
intro: This is under a mile of the Post Road through Old Lyme, from the Lieutenant River to Griswold Avenue. The river is tidal here and joins the Connecticut in its estuary, just above Long Island Sound.
Old Lyme was a shipbuilding village and home to many ship captains before the painters came. US 1 itself spent 1949 to 1976 out on the line of I-95, then came back to its old road.

moments.title: Florence Griswold Museum
moments.text: Miss Florence's boarding house by the Lieutenant River sheltered the Old Lyme Art Colony, whose painters left 41 panels on its doors and walls, and Childe Hassam painted the river from there.

moments.title: Peck Tavern
moments.text: At the junction of Sill Lane and the Post Road stands the old tavern, now a private house, where George Washington stopped in April 1776 and was seen dancing the night away upstairs.
